headline: S&P 500 drops 2.0% for a sixth straight loss as gold and silver sink to 52-week lows
subhead: Nasdaq fell 2.3% and the VIX jumped 15.8% to 28.44 as an early AI rally reversed despite Anthropic closing 17 percent above its 83 dollar IPO price; gold fell 3.3% to 3,618.5 and silver 4.8% to 42.8.

us.text: S&P 500 fell 2.0% to 7,175.8, its sixth straight loss and 8.2% below its 52-week high; the Dow lost 2.2% and the Nasdaq 2.3%.
Anthropic opened at 111.50 dollars and closed at 97.17, up 17 percent from its 83 dollar IPO price, worth about 1.28 trillion dollars.
AMD fell 7.7% on a Hunterbrook short report on China ties; Nvidia fell 3.3% and Alphabet 3.5%, both to 52-week lows.

india.text: Nifty rose 1.14% to 25,514.3 on Thursday and Bank Nifty closed at a record 63,063 on auto and bank buying; the price feed still shows Wednesday's 25,228.0, down 0.6%.
FIIs net bought 7,411.4 crore rupees in cash on Thursday while DIIs net sold 1,356.6 crore.
Rupee rose for a fourth session to 93.36 per dollar on foreign inflows; the feed shows 93.28, up 0.2%.

global.text: Nikkei 225 fell 2.2% to 57,722.8 on Friday and Samsung 4.2% as SoftBank and chip stocks slid after the US selloff.
Stoxx 600 fell 0.9% on Thursday, its longest losing streak since August, led by food, healthcare and real estate.
Hang Seng fell 1.95% to a four-month low of 22,841.6 on Thursday as Tencent dropped after a revenue miss.

weekly.narrative: Jensen Huang's sudden exit as Nvidia CEO dominated the week: Nvidia fell 12.8 percent, but rotation into Apple, AMD and Broadcom still left the S&P 500 up 2.5 percent and the Nasdaq up 2.3 percent despite a Friday AI selloff. Hot US CPI and 6.5 percent annual PPI pushed the 10-year yield to 5.15 percent and left a December Fed hike fully priced, lifting the dollar to a 19-month high. That weighed on metals and crypto: gold fell 4.5 percent to a 13-month low, silver 6.1 percent and bitcoin broke below 70,000 dollars. India leaned on nine straight sessions of foreign buying and a bank rally, though the Nifty slipped to 25,144.3 on Friday after October CPI rose to 6.09 percent. Next week brings Nvidia results on 17 November, FOMC minutes on 18 November and Anthropic's expected Nasdaq debut on 19 November.
